name: collection_index
description: List every object of a delivered collection: size, modified time (UTC, to the nanosecond the file system holds; modified_epoch_ns is the raw value as a decimal string, because a JSON number past 2^53 does not survive a JavaScript or jq 1.6 reader), the SHA-256 of the whole file, and a hypothesis for the path the file had on the source machine. source_path_hypothesis is a convention's reading of the path in the collection (path, method, confidence low, medium or none, the components it could not explain, the other readings): a guess about a layout, never called the original path; a real root directory is kept, a Linux tree is rooted the same way with or without it, and a wrapper that needs the collector's own index (uploads/<accessor>/...) is not decoded. source_path_observed is filled only from a collector's own record: a KAPE copy log in the tree, matched by the row's DestinationFile ending with the file's path relative to that log's own directory (so a file outside it never claims the row), with the log, the row and the log's ModifiedOnUtc raw beside the delivered time; rows that name one source are one observation, rows that name different sources, or a sibling that shares the name letters of case apart, are ambiguous with every candidate listed, and none is nothing; a copy log with rows it cannot use makes the mapping partial; no other collector's records are read. A disk image, a memory capture or an archive in the root is indexed like any file and says what it looks like (object_class, from its first bytes and name; nothing is opened). Symbolic links are recorded and never followed, special files and empty directories are recorded, and every object that could not be listed, examined or read is a row with its error and makes the status partial. The complete census is written to a file in a job, with out_file, with a contains filter, and whenever the inline page cannot hold it (a page is bounded by bytes as well as by limit); a file already at the name is never replaced (this one is kept beside it as name.2.jsonl and named) and an out_file inside the collection is refused, by identity, so a case-variant spelling does not get round it. contains is read on what is printed, never on a withheld text, filters the inline page and the hashing only (the file holds every object with matches_filter, and files outside the filter say not_attempted), and a pattern outside a small language (no repeated group, no back-reference or lookaround, at most one unbounded repetition, four | inside groups) is refused by name; a search of one name that takes more than 2 seconds stops the run with an error. More than 90% of more than 20 files on one UTC date is reported as mtime_distribution_anomaly with counts and no cause; the collector's recorded times, archive member times and the acquisition time are other clocks, not read here. possible_renamed_streams is a guess from file-name shape. Not measured: whether the tree is complete, whether a time is the source's or the copy's, a stream that was dropped. A name that marks a credential store (a password verifier file, a private key, a keychain, a saved-credential or browser store, DPAPI, hive logs; may_hold_secrets, a name hint only) is not hashed unless hash_credential_stores is true, which needs a job and write_values: true: its digest then goes only to the sealed values file, never to the answer or the index. Run it as a job with secret_output: true (the tool cannot see whether the job was run so). Paths are withheld where shaped like a recovery password, an access key, a token, a private-key block, URL user-info, or the value after a credential header, key name or password option; write_values: true (jobs only) writes the real strings to $OUT/collection-index-values.jsonl, mode 0600, created first, a second run in the same job refused. The answer starts with the summary and ends with the entries. Every key and value of the answer and of the table files it names is withheld by shape, and the structure is then read back by a second check written apart from the first; a string that check finds suspect is replaced by <withheld: N bytes>, counted in the answer's boundary entry, and the answer is partial. Withholding is by shape. Measured on random plants (1,000 per shape and context: alone, in a path, a file name, a log line, a URL, an option, glued to letters), the 33 listed shapes (token prefixes, JWT, PEM, connection strings, user-info, name=value and option forms, recovery passwords), the unlisted token families (GitLab, Stripe, Google, npm, SendGrid, DigitalOcean, Twilio), names such as DB_PASSWORD= and adminPassword:, and tokens split by NUL, zero-width, bidi, UTF-16-in-8-bit or full-width characters or written in another case come out in 0.2% or fewer of the plants; AWS-secret-shaped keys and base64 of 20 to 48 bytes in 0.7% or fewer, base64 of 16 bytes in 2.5%, 20 random letters and digits in 1.5% and 32 in 0.5%; base36 text of 24 to 32 characters in 18% to 26%. A plain password or passphrase alone in a name, a UUID-shaped key, 24 lower-case letters and 16 characters of base32 are printed (100%). A secret of another shape is printed: a file whose secrets matter is read in a secret_output job. Cost on real names, measured: 0.47% of this repository's paths, 0.14% of 37,916 Linux package paths and 3.64% of 57,142 macOS system and application paths (hardware ids and GUID-named profiles read as random) are withheld.

root.description: The collection directory (an archive is not opened: extract it into a job's output first)

contains.description: Case-insensitive regex (at most 2000 characters) over the path in the collection and over the hypothesis path. It filters the inline page and the hashing; the complete index file holds every object. Literals, ., [classes], ^ $, | and groups that are not repeated only, with at most one unbounded repetition, two {n,m}, four ? and four | inside groups; one search of one name that takes more than 2 seconds ends the run with an error

hash.description: Hash every matching file (default true; false is much faster on a large tree, and each row then says it was not attempted)

hash_credential_stores.description: Hash the files whose names mark a credential store too (default false). Refused unless the tool runs as a job, which must be run with secret_output: true; never copy such a digest into a post, a report or an indicator list

limit.description: Rows shown inline (default 200); the complete index is in the file complete_index names

out_file.description: Optional JSONL path for the complete index, under work/ (in a job, under $OUT); refused inside the collection, outside the run directory or under inputs/, and never replacing a file that is there (the result is kept beside it and named)

time_limit_seconds.description: Stop the census after this long (default 3000, at most 3400): the answer then says it stopped, status partial, and how many directories were not listed

write_values.description: Write the real strings that were withheld to $OUT/collection-index-values.jsonl (default false). Refused unless the tool runs as a job, which must be run with secret_output: true; the file is created first and one already there is refused
